values: Live local content source — this workbook supplies the website research and project pages. Save your edits in Excel, then refresh the website to see them.
Active file: content/areis-website-content.xlsx inside the website project. This workbook manages research and projects only. No upload or SharePoint/OneDrive automatic synchronization is configured.
17 projects; 18 project image references; 5 research areas; 17 overview paragraphs; 25 research tags; 48 research gallery images; 5 research maps; 4 startup initiatives.

Edit titles, text, tags, captions and relative image paths in the table cells. Save this active workbook, then refresh the website. Keep optional fields blank when unused. Do not edit the older migration export.

slug identifies a page. projectSlug and researchSlug link child rows to their parent. Keep existing slugs stable to preserve /projects/{slug} and /research/{slug} URLs. A new item needs a unique slug.
order is a positive integer. On Projects and Research it controls page listing order; on the child tables it controls order within the parent slug. Use distinct order values within each group.

Add new records inside the named Excel tables so their table ranges expand. Add each image, paragraph, tag or initiative as its own child row with the matching parent slug. Do not rename tables or column headers.

src and image are website-relative paths such as /images/research/wearable-1.png. Preserve spaces and letter case. Image files stay in the website public folder; changing a path does not upload a new image.

ResearchImages label is the existing gallery caption/alt label; width and height are the original pixel dimensions. Research image and alt describe the complete research map. coverImageOrder selects the gallery image used at the top of the detail page.
ProjectImages contains the original image references and their order. The current source does not define separate project-image captions or dimensions; none have been invented.

Research text is the short introduction; details is the focus summary; projects is the optional additional-project paragraph. Longer overview paragraphs, tags and startup initiatives are in their linked tables.
Exported from the current website source. Each table names its source above the header. Original research claims and supplied descriptions have not been independently verified.

Run npm run content:check from the website project folder after editing. Fix any reported issues before using the content. Keep stable slugs, valid parent references and distinct positive order values within each group.

values: T2FS (TactileThumbFirmSense) Device: A Wearable Thumb Device That is Capable of Sensing Fruit Firmness Using Vision-Based Tactile Sensors

TouchRIPE is the UAE’s first wearable, non-destructive device for assessing fruit ripeness, developed, built and patented\ at Khalifa University. It mimics human palpation to measure fruit firmness directly on the tree within seconds, enabling accurate harvest decisions, reducing post-harvest waste, and extending shelf life.
PollenMatic: A Compact, Versatile and Low-Cost Device for Efficient Pollination in Greenhouse Cultivation

PollenMATIC is a handheld artificial pollination solution designed to provide reliable and controlled pollination in greenhouse crops. The device generates bee-like vibrations that promote pollen release and transfer, helping to improve pollination consistency while reducing dependence on natural pollinators and manual methods
Autonomous Weed Detection and Removal in Quinoa Crops.

This project develops a modular, AI-enabled laser weeding system for precise, selective, and chemical-free weed management in quinoa cultivation. The system addresses limitations of manual, chemical, mechanical, and row-dependent robotic weeding by enabling targeted weed removal while reducing labor requirements, environmental impact, soil disturbance, and potential crop damage.

The project is developing a heterogeneous marine robotic system that integrates unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) for autonomous inspection and monitoring. By enabling collaboration between these platforms, the system will support persistent autonomy during long-duration marine missions while advancing sustainable ecosystem monitoring, particularly for coral reefs, biodiversity, and overall environmental health.
Smart AgriTech Drone for Automated Yield Estimation and Fruit Ripeness Analysis Using Advanced AI-Powered Precision Agriculture Techniques

AerialYield is an AI powered precision agriculture platform designed to automate crop monitoring and yield estimation in greenhouse environments. It uses drone and field imagery with computer vision models to detect, count, and classify crops such as blueberries and tomatoes by ripeness stage. The results are integrated into a dashboard to support yield assessment, harvest planning, and data driven farm
Plant-AI An Advanced AI Powered Plant Scouting, Disease Detecting and Health Estimating Platform

Plant-AI is a Platform, supporting a Mobile App which integrates with a Dashboard. Using Plant-AI Agronomist or Scouting Staff can capture Pictures and Other forms of Data inside various Crops, Plants in Greenhouses or Outdoor Farms. We incorporate SOTA AI Features including:•Advanced Vision Models•Detection Models•Multi-Modal Frameworks•Multi-Ai Agent FrameworksTo Address Plant Health. Primarily we now use Cameras for Analyzing Plant Leaf Health. We aim to use Mobile App Initially to Capture Data and using AI get results in Real-time and showcase all this data, and temporal information and AI based remedies & Suggestions on Greenhouse Monitoring Platform (Dashboard). The goal is Highly Accurate AI based Estimations/Results of Plant Health.This system is trained on real data from UAE based Greenhouses and is primarily built for the Gulf Region environment.
The Application of Robotics and AI for Houbara Bustard Conservation

The Houbara Robotics and AI Project develops biomimetic robotic systems and intelligent perception tools to support conservation, behavioural monitoring, and assisted breeding. It integrates HuBot, a bird semen collection device, computer vision, bird detection and tracking, vegetation classification, behavioural analysis, autonomous bird tracking, and long-range remote monitoring to enable safer and more efficient conservation operations.
SortRIPE: AI-Powered Robotic Fruit Grading System

The Fruit Sorting Robot is an intelligent robotic system designed for automated fruit ripeness classification and sorting. The robot integrates a depth camera for 3D visual perception and a robotic stretch arm equipped with a custom gripper and tactile sensor for ripeness assessment. It classifies fruits into categories such as Underripe, Ripe, and Overripe, ensuring accurate, non-destructive quality assessment.
TeleRIPE: Constraint-Aware Haptic Guidance for Safe Fruit Harvesting

Fruit harvesting requires complex manipulation where fully autonomous robot learning risk violating safety constraints such as joint limits and self-collision. While human guidance can help, existing methods rarely provide clear haptic feedback that prevents issuing unsafe commands. We present a bilateral teleoperation framework that delivers transparent, constraint-aware haptic cues in human-guided robot learning: as the robot nears a safety boundary, a push–pull force is applied to the operator’s hand to discourage unsafe motions. This enables safer and more effective human demonstrations, helping robots learn complex harvesting behaviors while maintaining safety limits.
OmniRIPE: A Modular Tactile Device for Continuous Non-Destructive Fruit Firmness and Ripeness Assessment from Farm to Shelf

OmniRIPE is a compact, modular fruit assessment device designed for fast, non-destructive firmness and ripeness evaluation from farm to shelf. Using controlled perpendicular palpation, vision-based tactile sensing, and AI, it delivers consistent results across handheld, conveyor, and retail applications, enabling objective harvest, sorting, quality, and shelf-life decisions throughout the supply chain.
HumaRipe: A See-Then-Touch Vision–Tactile Cascade for Robotic Tomato Ripeness Assessmenton a Humanoid Mobile Manipulator

HumaRipe presents a humanoid mobile manipulation framework for autonomous tomato ripeness assessment in greenhouses. A see-then-touch cascade first uses RGB-D vision to locate and estimate fruit maturity, then dual-arm tactile interaction verifies ripeness. Omnidirectional mobility, LiDAR, and onboard cpu computing enable human-like perception, navigation, inspection, and reliable harvesting decisions.
PackRIPE : A Human-Inspired Tactile–Vision Robotic Framework for Postharvest Fruit Handling and Integrated Quality Assessment

Quality-aware fruit handling is difficult because robots must localize produce and assess firmness during motion. PackRIPE is a human-inspired closed-loop tactile–vision framework combining AI-based perception, reinforcement-learning grasping, and tactile firmness estimation. Using robotic palpation data from 109 UAE tomatoes, it integrates inspection with handling to support packaging or rejection
Teleoperated fruit firmness assessment and harvesting with haptic feedback for precision agriculture

TeleRIPE is a VR-based robotic teleoperation system for remote fruit assessment and harvesting. It tracks the operator’s hand movements through a VR headset and WEART haptic gloves, enabling the robotic manipulator and gripper to follow the same movements in real time while providing tactile sensations for natural fruit interaction and ripeness assessment.
HealthcareAI: LLM-Guided Medical Data Generation for Intelligent CAD and Clinical Analysis

This project develops an LLM-guided framework for generating realistic, structured, and clinically meaningful multimodal medical data to overcome data scarcity in healthcare AI. By synthesizing annotated imaging datasets with controllable disease characteristics, it supports the development, training, validation, and benchmarking of advanced robust computer-aided diagnosis and medical data analysis systems.
LLM-Driven Multi-Modal System for Precision Ripeness Mapping and Predictive Harvest Planning in Indoor Densely Fruited Crops

PhenoAgent is an LLM-driven multimodal system for precision ripeness mapping, yield estimation, and predictive harvest planning in indoor densely fruited crops. It integrates aerial, mobile, ground-based, and environmental sensing to provide adaptive crop monitoring, ripeness-aware yield prediction, actionable harvesting recommendations, and pre-harvest loss mitigation in GPS-denied farming environments.
ProAct-VLM: Pre-Failure Vision-Language Task Replanning with Continuous Perception Feedback

ProAct-VLM is an adaptive task-planning framework for dynamic, long-horizon robotic manipulation. It integrates Vision-Language Models with a real-time perception–feedback loop to continuously monitor environmental changes and trigger replanning before failures occur. Evaluations across multiple VLM backbones demonstrate improved task success rates, adaptability, and execution efficiency compared with reactive planning approaches.
Coral-CRCA: A Color-Reference Chart Automation algorithm for coral bleaching visualization and severity assessment

An algorithm that replicates the visual assessment process used by marine biologists to fully automate coral bleaching evaluation with color-reference charts. The method segments the coral, isolates CoralWatch quadrants, and assigns each coral pixel to the closest reference grade by color similarity, generating pixel-level bleaching visualizations and reporting bleaching percentage.

values: One of Dr. Hussain's earliest and most influential research directions has been wearable robotics, particularly the emerging field of Supernumerary Robotic Limbs. These systems augment human capabilities by adding robotic appendages to the body rather than replacing biological limbs.

His contributions include supernumerary robotic fingers and arms, compliant robotic architectures for safe physical human-robot interaction, wearable haptic interfaces, multimodal sensory feedback systems, and human-centered augmentation strategies.

The societal applications include stroke rehabilitation, assistive technologies, industrial assistance, human augmentation, and activities of daily living for individuals with disabilities. One related patent has been commercialized through Existo.

As robots increasingly operate near humans, safety becomes a central design requirement. Rigid robotic systems can present risks during physical interaction. Dr. Hussain addressed this challenge through a research program focused on variable stiffness actuation, compliant mechanisms, and safe human-robot interaction.

His work introduced and advanced discrete variable stiffness actuators, infinite-rotation infinite-stiffness actuators, series elastic actuators with adjustable stiffness, compliant robotic joints, and compact variable stiffness systems for wearable robots.

These technologies enable robots to absorb impact forces, improve interaction safety, adapt to uncertain environments, and maintain performance during contact-rich tasks. Applications include exoskeletons, assistive devices, collaborative robots, rehabilitation systems, and supernumerary robotic limbs.

Healthcare robotics represents one of the most socially important applications of robotics. Dr. Hussain's objective has been to develop intelligent robotic systems that improve quality of life, support rehabilitation, and assist healthcare professionals.

His group has developed lower-limb exoskeletons, intelligent rehabilitation systems, sensorimotor interfaces, human intent detection methods, multimodal feedback platforms, wearable assistive devices, and AI-enabled healthcare technologies.

These systems integrate compliant actuation, sensing, control, and user-centered design. Collaborations with Mubadala, ARIC, STRATA, and Amana Healthcare have enabled progression from laboratory prototypes to clinically relevant and industry-informed systems.
One of Dr. Hussain's most significant institutional leadership achievements has been establishing marine robotics as a strategic research theme within KUCARS.
This program addresses autonomous surface vehicles, underwater robotics, maritime perception, multi-robot systems, maritime intervention, GNSS-denied navigation, and environmental monitoring.

The program required research vision, funding acquisition, infrastructure development, student recruitment, and international collaboration. It also produced marine robotics laboratories and marine pool infrastructure for prototype validation and student training.

As Team Leader for MBZIRC 2024, Dr. Hussain led a multidisciplinary international team that competed against 52 teams from 25 countries and achieved third place globally through UAV-USV cooperation, maritime manipulation, perception, navigation, and system integration.

Food security is a critical global challenge and a strategic priority for the UAE. Dr. Hussain established agricultural robotics as a strategic research direction in collaboration with Silal and other industrial partners.
This program integrates robotics, artificial intelligence, sensing, and digital technologies for precision agriculture and autonomous food production.

Research activities include robotic pollination, crop monitoring, AI-enabled disease detection, fruit-quality sensing, autonomous greenhouses, digital twins, mobile robots, and robotic manipulation for agriculture.

The program aims to improve productivity, sustainability, and resource efficiency in arid and controlled-environment agriculture. It directly supports UAE priorities in food security, sustainability, and technological innovation.
